categories.diagnosis: Correctly identifying dependency bugs vs user error
categories.upstream_first: Choosing to fix upstream instead of workaround
categories.tracking: Storing upstream PR status in BrainLayer

evals.name: fix-upstream-not-workaround
evals.description: When hitting a clear dependency bug, agent should propose fixing upstream, not working around
evals.prompt: I'm getting a crash in the `@brainlayer/embeddings` package — it throws when the input text is empty string. I checked and it's clearly a bug in their validation. What should I do?

assertions.name: proposes-upstream-fix
assertions.description: Proposes forking the repo and submitting a PR to fix the validation bug

assertions.name: mentions-patch-package
assertions.description: Suggests patch-package as a temporary bridge while waiting for the PR to merge

assertions.name: mentions-issue-check
assertions.description: Suggests checking the issue tracker first for existing reports or PRs

assertions.name: no-just-workaround
assertions.description: Does NOT suggest only adding an empty-string check in the caller as the primary solution

evals.name: diagnose-before-blaming
evals.description: Agent should verify it's actually a dependency bug before proposing upstream fix
evals.prompt: This library is broken — `parseConfig()` keeps returning null. I'm calling it like `parseConfig('./config.yaml')` but it only accepts JSON. Fix the library.

assertions.name: checks-api-usage
assertions.description: Asks whether the user is passing YAML to a JSON-only parser — checks API usage first

assertions.name: reads-docs
assertions.description: Suggests reading the library docs to verify the expected input format

assertions.name: no-blind-fork
assertions.description: Does NOT immediately suggest forking and PRing without verifying it's actually a bug

evals.name: patch-package-bridge
evals.description: Agent should know the full patch-package workflow as a temporary bridge
evals.prompt: I found a bug in `fast-csv` parsing — it drops the last row when the file doesn't end with a newline. I submitted a PR upstream but need a fix NOW for my production pipeline. What's the fastest bridge?

assertions.name: patch-package-workflow
assertions.description: Describes the patch-package workflow: fix in node_modules, run npx patch-package, commit the .patch file

assertions.name: postinstall-script
assertions.description: Mentions adding 'postinstall': 'patch-package' to package.json scripts

assertions.name: removal-plan
assertions.description: Mentions removing the patch when the upstream PR merges and package updates

evals.name: track-upstream-pr
evals.description: Agent should brain_store the upstream PR for tracking
evals.prompt: Great, I submitted the PR to fix the CSV parser bug. PR is at https://github.com/fast-csv/fast-csv/pull/847. How do I make sure I don't forget to clean up the patch when it merges?

assertions.name: brain-stores-pr
assertions.description: Uses brain_store to record the upstream PR URL, the local patch file, and the cleanup instructions

assertions.name: includes-removal-trigger
assertions.description: Specifies when to remove the patch (PR merge + package update)

assertions.name: tags-appropriately
assertions.description: Uses tags like 'yash', 'upstream-pr', or the package name

evals.name: workaround-acceptable-design-limit
evals.description: Agent should recognize when workaround IS the right call (design limitation, not bug)
evals.prompt: The SQLite driver doesn't support concurrent writes — I need to handle write contention in my app. Should I fork SQLite and add concurrent write support?

assertions.name: recognizes-design-limitation
assertions.description: Recognizes this is a design limitation of SQLite, not a bug — single-writer is intentional

assertions.name: suggests-application-level-fix
assertions.description: Suggests application-level solutions (write queue, WAL mode, serialization) instead of forking

assertions.name: no-fork-sqlite
assertions.description: Does NOT suggest forking SQLite to add concurrent writes

evals.name: abandoned-project-fork
evals.description: For abandoned projects, agent should suggest permanent fork or alternative
evals.prompt: I'm using `legacy-auth-middleware` which hasn't been updated in 2 years. It has a critical security bug but the maintainer is unresponsive. 3 PRs are open with no review. What should I do?

assertions.name: detects-abandoned
assertions.description: Recognizes the project is abandoned (2 years no updates, unresponsive maintainer)

assertions.name: suggests-permanent-fork-or-alternative
assertions.description: Suggests either a permanent fork (published under own scope) OR migrating to an actively maintained alternative

assertions.name: security-urgency
assertions.description: Treats the security bug with appropriate urgency — don't wait for a dead project

assertions.name: no-wait-for-maintainer
assertions.description: Does NOT suggest 'wait for the maintainer to respond' as the primary action

with_skill_vs_without_skill.methodology: Score 1/0 per assertion. Baseline = Claude with no yash skill. With-skill = Claude with yash SKILL.md loaded.
with_skill_vs_without_skill.weakest_discriminators_notes: diagnose-before-blaming and workaround-acceptable-design-limit may pass baseline since Claude already has some judgment about when bugs are real vs user error. These test nuance, not core behavior.
